title: OpenAI & AARP Launch Free ChatGPT Workshops for Seniors
summary: OpenAI partners with AARP to deliver hands-on ChatGPT training to 1,000 older adults in 10 U.S. cities, building practical AI skills for everyday life.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- OpenAI and AARP are delivering free, hands-on ChatGPT workshops to 1,000 older adults in 10 U.S. cities starting this fall.
- The program addresses digital literacy gaps, teaching seniors to use AI safely for health research, trip planning, and everyday tasks.
- Workshops emphasize privacy, misinformation detection, and building confidence in AI tools through peer learning and expert guidance.


OpenAI and AARP have joined forces to deliver free, in-person ChatGPT workshops to 1,000 older adults across 10 U.S. cities this fall. The partnership addresses a growing need for digital literacy among Americans aged 50 and older, many of whom feel excluded from the AI revolution reshaping daily life. Officially launched on September 16, 2026, the program combines hands-on training with safety education to help seniors confidently navigate generative AI tools.


## Workshop Structure and Location Rollout


The initiative spans 10 metropolitan areas, including New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Houston, and Phoenix. Each two-hour session accommodates 15 to 25 participants and follows a structured curriculum developed by OpenAI's education team and AARP's digital literacy experts. Attendees receive printed guides, one-on-one troubleshooting support, and follow-up resources for continued learning at home.


Sessions emphasize practical applications: researching health conditions, planning travel itineraries, drafting emails, and exploring hobbies. Instructors demonstrate ChatGPT's interface step-by-step, addressing common barriers like account setup, mobile versus desktop usage, and interpreting AI-generated responses. AARP volunteer coordinators facilitate small-group exercises to reinforce concepts through peer learning.


## Addressing Safety and Misinformation Concerns


A core component of the curriculum focuses on responsible AI use. Workshops dedicate 30 minutes to identifying misinformation, understanding privacy settings, and recognizing when to verify AI outputs with authoritative sources. OpenAI's team stresses that ChatGPT is a tool for exploration, not a replacement for professional advice in medical, legal, or financial contexts.


Participants learn to spot hallucinations (fabricated information), cross-reference facts using traditional search engines, and protect personal data by avoiding sensitive inputs. AARP's fraud prevention specialists contribute modules on phishing scams that exploit AI-generated content, equipping seniors with red flags to watch for in emails and messages.


## Bridging the Digital Divide


The program directly responds to research showing 40 percent of Americans over 65 feel uncomfortable with emerging technologies. Many older adults report anxiety about "breaking" software or making irreversible mistakes, a fear compounded by rapidly evolving AI interfaces. By offering guided, judgment-free environments, the workshops aim to build confidence through repetition and success.


- Free loaner tablets provided during sessions for participants without smartphones
- Multilingual support in Spanish, Mandarin, and Tagalog in select cities
- Optional follow-up virtual office hours for troubleshooting after workshops conclude


AARP's community centers serve as primary venues, leveraging existing trust relationships with older populations. OpenAI contributes funding for venue costs, instructor stipends, and printed materials, while AARP handles logistics, registration, and volunteer recruitment.


## Measuring Impact and Future Expansion


OpenAI plans to survey participants six weeks post-workshop to assess retention, frequency of ChatGPT use, and perceived value. Early pilot data from a June 2026 trial in Portland showed 78 percent of attendees continued using the tool weekly, primarily for recipe searches, correspondence drafting, and news summarization. Positive outcomes could trigger expansion to 50 additional cities by mid-2027.


The partnership also explores train-the-trainer models, empowering local AARP volunteers to lead workshops independently after certification. This scalability approach mirrors successful digital literacy campaigns AARP has run for online banking and telehealth adoption over the past decade.


## What This Means for AI Accessibility


This collaboration signals a broader industry shift toward inclusive design and education. As AI tools permeate healthcare, government services, and consumer applications, ensuring older adults can participate prevents a two-tier society where access to information and efficiency depends on age. OpenAI's investment in grassroots training complements technical improvements, acknowledging that user confidence matters as much as interface simplicity. For seniors willing to engage, AI offers practical shortcuts to independence, from managing medications to staying connected with distant family, provided the learning curve is met with patience and support.
